sections.content: A register is the level of formality you choose. The same message changes with the situation: a message to a friend, a conversation with a client, a letter to an office. You already have the tools: *tú* or *usted* (this unit), the polite forms of A2 Unit 26 and B2 Unit 2, and the formal requests of the last lesson. This lesson puts them side by side.

sections.title: Same message, two registers
rows: Hola, ¿qué tal? / Buenos días, ¿cómo está usted?
Dame tu número. / ¿Me daría su número, por favor?
Give me your number. / Would you give me your number, please?
Te escribo mañana. / Le escribiré mañana.
Que te vaya bien. / Que tenga un buen día.

sections.content: Four things change: the pronoun and verb (*tú* → *usted*), the softening (a plain request → *¿me daría…?*), the greeting and the farewell. You can also switch in the middle of a conversation: from *usted* to *tú* when the other person offers it, and back to *usted* when you enter a formal setting, such as an office or a letter.
When in doubt, start with *usted*. It is easy to move to *tú* when invited; it is awkward to move the other way.
